mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for 4 consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from a pre-rate hike period (p > 0.05) or the 60-day moving average of 20-day returns turns positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by at least 2,000 in two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a statistically significant positive regression coefficient for the interaction term (p < 0.05) in a 200-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand composition toward services, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth exceeds 3% while INDPRO monthly decline exceeds 2% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from goods to services dominance
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain negative even after controlling for lagged GDPC1 and INDPRO (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede a sharp S&P 500 drawdown; thus, 20-day forward returns are expected to be negative.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.01) during the identified contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate a rate hike cycle.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during the inflation spike (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (proxy: HOUST) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 500 in a single month while UNRATE remains below 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite a significant positive interaction effect (p < 0.05) in a 180-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (implied via negative PAYEMS trend) coupled with rising consumer confidence ( proxy: not available in evidence, so skip or use alternative ) — instead, use: declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising payrolls (PAYEMS) as a contradictory demand signal; however, to stay evidence-grounded, let's use: A decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) while GDP momentum (not available) — so instead, use: A sustained decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) for 4 months predicts negative 20-day forward returns as it signals weak demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the four-month decline period.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling industrial production (INDPRO) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3%), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 60 days as supply-side pressures and cost-push inflation erode profit margins.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% and INDPRO decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive with a robust positive coefficient for the interaction term (p < 0.01) in a multiple regression.
